title: Koszul orthogonality detects extension from an open
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let j:U \to X be an open immersion, let V=Spec(A) be an affine open of X, and suppose X=U union V with U intersection V quasi-compact. Put Z=V minus U, choose f_1, ..., f_r in A with Z=V(f_1, ..., f_r), and let K be the bounded Koszul complex whose degree-q term is the q-th exterior power of A^r and whose differential is contraction with (f_1, ..., f_r), viewed as a perfect object of D(O_V) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex]. For every E in D_QCoh(O_V) [def-pc-derived-category], the following are equivalent: (i) the canonical map E \to R(U intersection V \to V)_*(E restricted to U intersection V) is an isomorphism; (ii) Hom(K[n],E)=0 for every integer n.

proof.text: Identify a⁻¹U with the union of the basic opens using the given zero-locus equivalence. For K the stated sheafified Koszul object, lem-pc-koszul-restriction-zero gives F(K[n])=0. The supplied adjunction homEquiv makes Hom(K[n],R(F(E))) a subsingleton for each n. If the unit is invertible, postcomposition is injective, hence Hom(K[n],E) is a subsingleton.
Choose a distinguished triangle E→R(F(E))→C→E[1] by Mathlib Pretriangulated.distinguished_cocone_triangle. The derived open-unit cone lemma supplies quasi-coherent cohomology of C and F(C)=0.

Assume all Hom(K[n],E) vanish. The adjunction of shifts identifies Hom(K[n],E[1]) with Hom(K[n−1],E), hence it vanishes. For v:K[n]→C its composite to E[1] is zero, so Triangle.coyoneda_exact₃ factors it through R(F(E)). That Hom group vanishes by the first step, so v=0. Apply positive-power propagation to obtain vanishing against all Koszul powers.

Apply isZero_of_koszul_powers_orthogonal to the full-subcategory object ⟨C,hC⟩, with the open identified in step 1, zero restriction, and power orthogonality from step 3. This proves C is zero. Triangle.isZero₃_iff_isIso₁ then makes the original unit invertible.
